subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: The reactants
hotspots.description: The hydrogen molecules (two pale spheres each) and oxygen molecule (two red spheres) on the left are the reactants — the starting materials of the reaction.
hotspots.positionHint: The molecule group on the left side of the equation.
hotspots.function: Shows the starting materials of the reaction.

hotspots.label: Reacting together
hotspots.description: When the combine layer is on, the reactants approach and react — their atoms break apart and reconnect as water.
hotspots.positionHint: The central region where the molecules meet when the layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the reactants coming together to react.

hotspots.label: Consumed and transformed
hotspots.description: As the reaction runs, the reactant atoms are consumed — not destroyed — and reappear rearranged as the water product on the right.
hotspots.positionHint: The atoms flowing from the left molecules into the water product.
hotspots.function: Shows reactants being consumed into products.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A miniature chemical equation floats centered — reactants on the left, an arrow, a product on the right — lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Ball-stick molecules in CPK colors: hydrogen warm off-white, oxygen muted red. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (amber / molecular-green / coral accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Hydrogen spheres: warm off-white, roughness ~0.5. Oxygen spheres: muted red, roughness ~0.45. Bond rods: thin graphite cylinders. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: a chemical equation for making water, built to be read as 'left side = reactants, right side = products.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a flat equation scene — LEFT: two hydrogen molecules (H₂, pairs of warm off-white spheres radius ~0.2 with a thin graphite rod) and one oxygen molecule (O₂, pair of muted red spheres radius ~0.28 with a double rod); CENTER: a flat arrow tile (app-rendered arrow glyph, no mesh text); RIGHT: one water molecule (H₂O, one muted red + two warm off-white, 104.5° bend).

2) COMBINE (toggleable layer): the hydrogen and oxygen molecules glide toward the center (app animates), their bonds break, and the atoms reassemble into water molecules at the right — the reaction visible as a dance of atoms.

3) ARROW (toggleable layer): the central arrow tile brightens and gains a soft glow, emphasizing 'reacts to make' — the divider between reactants and products.

Camera: framed so all three zones (left, center, right) fit with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: Reactant_H2_01-02, Reactant_O2, Product_H2O, EquationArrow, AtomTrails. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
